summary: An excerpt from 'Book 10 — part 69', a fiction passage about a couple, Damian and Trish. Damian comforts a distressed Trish, putting her to bed, arranging a personal day and a visit to Jory and his family, and a walk in the hills. The passage then shifts to their last date, where Trish reveals she is returning to Washington, and Damian helps her pack her office over takeout-style Mexican food and banter about being 'Hill Rats'. The note also includes an unrelated-seeming aside about the 1880s-era 'Impression, Sunrise' painting being seen up close by Katie in 2013.
one_line: Excerpt from a novel in which Damian comforts Trish, then helps her pack her office when she decides to return to Washington.
key_facts: Damian puts Trish in fluffy jammies, wipes away her makeup with a cool face-cloth, and squeezes each of her fingernails the way she likes.
Damian says he will call the department secretary to tell him Trish is taking a personal day and will be in tomorrow.
Damian plans for Trish to see Jory and his family so she can see the boy whose life she saved.
The note states that in 2013, the original 'Impression, Sunrise' painting was seen up close by Katie, finally, after waiting in line for hours.
Trish tells Damian, 'Damian, you're a wonder,' and Damian replies, 'You inspire me, darling.'
Their thirty-fifth date was their last.
When Damian sees boxes in her office, he says, 'You're going back to Washington.' Trish answers, 'Yes.'
Trish realizes that everyone in the law department likely knew she had decided to go back to the Hill, while Damian had only suspected it until that instant.
Damian responds to the news with a brave face belied by the Fret wrinkles in his forehead.
Trish says she did not want to tell Damian over the phone once she had decided.
Damian asks whether she wants to come out for dinner with him, and she says the movers are coming in the morning.
Damian offers to get burger king or taco bell, and Trish chooses Mexican, saying 'taco bell'.
Damian lets Trish pay for dinner, saying, 'You're making the big bucks now.'
Damian packs carefully, padding her framed pictures and wrapping knick-knacks in individual sheets of spun fiber.
Damian reminds Trish that she always said 'Hill Rats were Hill Rats for life.'
